DEFAULT_MODE selects the profile the machine boots in, so the driver reports what the EC says rather than assuming balanced. Read live on 2026-09-23 as 0x9D, bit 4 set, i.e. Gaming, matching the owner's "the BIOS default is Gaming" (windows/vendor-ec-map.md; registers.yaml BIOS_OEM_2). Not made volatile: it is already cacheable at 5a24248, nothing writes it while the machine runs, and making it volatile would change what the HID lightbar and the China-mode path see.

The 16-entry curve is NOT replayed, and that is the issue's instruction plus a second reason of its own. registers.yaml has no entry for 0x0F00, which is why registers_status is empty and rule 3 requires it to be: the status this repository would have to cite does not exist. The mechanism is decoded rather than unknown, so a follow-up starts from it -- EC handler at bank0 0x888D, magic 0xFD/0xC9, selector 0x0F5F in 1..3 (1=Turbo, 2=Gaming, 3=Office), two 48-byte CODE tables to 0x0F00 and 0x0F30, selector 3 additionally split by 0x0782 bit 2, CODE base seeded 0x60F2 at 0x8653 (ec/annotations/manual-fan-ctrl-0751.md 6). The second reason: that handshake needs EC_ADDR_AP_OEM bit 0 CLEAR, which is the state in which the EC's unresolved PL clear at 0xA833 can fire. The consequence is stated in the PR body: the curve does not follow the mode.

The cTGP/DynamicBoost block is out of scope (issue #8), and keeping it out keeps this patch clear of the 25-vs-15-vs-5 W DynamicBoost disagreement, which is a cTGP-init question rather than a profile one. It is `confirmed-working` and the profile still does not write it, because the vendor writes identical bytes in all three modes -- there is nothing per-mode for a profile to switch.

NEVER WRITTEN, and that is the invariant the whole PL replay rests on. The EC zeroes 0x0783-0x0785 on the arm where this bit is CLEAR, and the fan-curve handshake parks the EC in exactly that state (ec/annotations/manual-fan-ctrl-0751.md 6). The driver sets this bit once from uniwill_ec_init() and the profile never touches it, so writing the power limits is safe rather than merely convenient. check_power_profile.py rule 8 fails the patch if 0x0741 ever appears in a write.

Fan Boost is bit 6 and the OEM service adds it while boost is on (SetFanMode, :1948; windows/vendor-ec-map.md). The profile writes bits 0-5 and 7 only, through FAN_PROFILE_MASK, so the OSD keeps sole ownership of bit 6 and two writers never share one byte. The EC itself clears this bit on a temperature arm (0x8990, registers.yaml MANUAL_FAN_CTRL item 2), which is a third writer and a reason the mode byte is declared volatile rather than cached.
